note: THE WORKTREE-FRESHNESS CHECK IS INERT ON EVERY MAC, AND IT ERRORS LOUDLY ENOUGH TO LOOK LIKE IT RAN. Found by The Prospect, 2026-09-01, while taking a worktree. WHAT YOU SEE: make worktree-take succeeds, the worktree is fine, and three lines of stderr scroll past -- syntax error near unexpected token newline at line 174, then w: unbound variable at line 142. Easy to read as cosmetic. IT IS NOT COSMETIC. macOS ships GNU bash 3.2.57 and there is no newer bash on this box; the script is #!/usr/bin/env bash so it gets 3.2, and the repo already knows it cannot run there -- scripts/subfloor-run-chunked.sh line 113 says in its own words that test-worktree-freshness.sh does not even PARSE under 3.2. So the script does not fail a check, it fails to BE a check: the thing it exists to guarantee (its header: a worktree must never serve a binary) is unprotected on the primary development machine, and has been since at least 2026-08-23 when d8fbabd71 last touched it. WHY IT SURVIVED: it is invoked from worktree-take, which SUCCEEDS anyway, so the errors are pure stderr noise attached to a green outcome. Nobody chases stderr on a command that worked. That is the same shape as game-check reporting a truncated failure list -- the observing tool answering a neighbouring question, here: did the command exit 0, rather than did the check run. WHAT TO DO: either install a modern bash on the Macs and point the shebang at it, or port the script to 3.2 (the last commit d8fbabd71 was already doing bash 3.2 work, so this may be a half-finished port rather than a design choice), or have worktree-take REFUSE rather than warn when the freshness script cannot execute. The third is cheapest and turns a silent gap into a loud one. NOT FIXED BY US -- out of scope for the campaign that found it, captured so the next reader does not have to re-derive why the stderr is there.
